source.title: Open Problems in the Topology of Manifolds

accepted.question_text: Let C4 = ⟨σ⟩ act freely on S2 × S2 by σ(x, y) = (y, −x), let M be the quotient manifold, let RP2 = S2/∼ embed in M by [x] ↦ [x, x], let N be the tangent disk bundle neighborhood of that RP2, and let M′ = N ∪ MCyl(L(4,1) → L(8,3)). Since M = N ∪ MCyl(L(4,1) → L(8,1)) and M′ is homotopy equivalent to M, are M and M′ homeomorphic, and are they diffeomorphic?

evidence.quote: Let C4 =⟨σ⟩ act freely on S2× S2 with that action of σ defined by the equation σ (x,y) = (y,−x) and let M be the quotient manifold.
The smooth manifold M′ = N∪MCyl(L(4,1)→ L(8,3)) is homotopy equivalent to M. Question. Are M and M′ homeomorphic? diffeomorphic?

accepted.question_text: For a trisection of a closed 4-manifold, identify properties that can be detected from local information such as a trisection diagram and that have strong global topological consequences analogous to Casson–Gordon theory for Heegaard splittings, where failure of strong irreducibility forces either reducibility of the splitting or the existence of an incompressible surface of positive genus.

evidence.quote: Casson and Gordon [1] was the notion of strong irreducibility, with their main theorem stating that if a closed 3–manifold has a splitting that is not strongly irreducible, then either the splitting is reducible or the manifold contains an incompressible surface of positive genus.

The challenge for the analogous theory of trisections of 4–manifold is to determine properties of trisections that have strong topological consequences and that can be determined by local information, for instance, from a trisection diagram.

accepted.question_text: Let M be a closed aspherical manifold whose fundamental group has nontrivial centre. Does there exist a finite cover of M that admits a principal S1-action?
accepted.context_brief: Aspherical manifolds with central fundamental group

evidence.quote: Given a closed aspherical manifold M whose fundamental group has nontrivial centre, we can ask the following: Question A. Does there exist a finite cover of M with a principal S1-action?

accepted.question_text: Let M be a closed aspherical manifold whose fundamental group has nontrivial centre. Is M null-cobordant?
accepted.context_brief: Aspherical manifolds with central fundamental group

evidence.quote: Given a closed aspherical manifold M whose fundamental group has nontrivial centre, we can ask the following: ... Question B. Is such an M null-cobordant?

accepted.question_text: If the trisection genus of a closed smooth 4-manifold M is the minimal genus of the central surface appearing in a trisection of M, is this trisection genus additive under connected sum?

evidence.quote: Let M be a closed smooth 4-manifold. The “trisection genus” of M is the minimal genus of the central surface appearing in a trisection of M. Question. Is the trisection genus additive under connected sum?

accepted.question_text: Which groups π for which topological surgery makes the Borel conjecture valid in this setting—for example elementary amenable groups—can occur as fundamental groups of compact aspherical 4-manifolds with boundary?

evidence.quote: By topological surgery, the Borel Conjecture is valid when the fundamental group π = π1(M0)∼= π1(M1) is good, for example, if π is elementary amenable. One now proceeds to the following three problems: 1. Decide which good π are the fundamental groups of compact aspherical 4-manifolds.

accepted.question_text: For compact aspherical 4-manifolds with boundary, which groups can occur as the fundamental groups of the boundary components?

evidence.quote: One now proceeds to the following three problems: ... 2. Determine the possible fundamental groups of the boundary components.

accepted.question_text: For compact aspherical 4-manifolds with boundary, which homeomorphism types can occur for the boundary components?

evidence.quote: One now proceeds to the following three problems: ... 3. Determine the homeomorphism types of the boundary components.

accepted.question_text: Let M be a closed smooth aspherical 4-manifold. Is every smooth 4-manifold that is homotopy equivalent to M necessarily diffeomorphic to M?

evidence.quote: Question. Let M be a closed smooth aspherical 4-manifold. Is every smooth 4-manifold homotopy equivalent to M diffeomorphic to M?
The question has not been answered for any M, not even the 4-torus.

accepted.question_text: Let Σ be an integral homology 3-sphere that is not homeomorphic to S3. Does there exist a locally flat embedding Σ ↪ S4 such that at least one of the complementary regions, or both of them, is not simply connected?

evidence.quote: Question. Let Σ be an integral homology 3-sphere, not homeomorphic to S 3. Is there a locally flat embedding Σ ↪→ S4 such that one or both complementary regions are not simply-connected?

accepted.question_text: If L is a stably slice link in S3 with more than one component and sn(L) denotes the least n such that the components of L bound disjoint locally flat nullhomologous disks in D4 # n(S2 × S2), must the inequality sn(L) ≤ g4^top(L) hold, where g4^top(L) is the topological 4-genus?

evidence.quote: A link L⊂ S3 is stably slice if there exists n≥ 0 such that the components of L bound a collection of disjoint locally flat nullhomologous discs in the manifold D4#n(S2× S2). The stabilising number sn(L) of a stably slice link is the minimal such n.
Question A. Does the inequality sn(L)≤ gtop 4 (L) hold for stably slice links L of more than one component?

accepted.question_text: Is there a knot K with Arf invariant zero that is not topologically slice and for which the topological stabilising number and smooth stabilising number differ, more precisely with 0 < sntop(K) < snsmooth(K)?

evidence.quote: Question B. Is there a difference between the topological and smooth stabilising numbers of a knot? More precisely, is there a non-topological slice, Arf invariant zero knot K such that 0 < sntop(K) < snsmooth(K) ?

accepted.question_text: Give a satisfactory proof of the statement that any two locally flat topological embeddings of a closed oriented surface in S4 whose complement has infinite cyclic fundamental group are homeomorphic.
accepted.context_brief: Proof problem for unknotted oriented surfaces in S4

evidence.quote: Kawauchi has published several accounts of the theorem below; however, none of them are satisfactory. The problem is to give a satisfactory proof.
Theorem. Any two locally flat topological embeddings of a closed oriented surface in S4 whose complement has infinite cyclic fundamental group are homeomorphic.

accepted.question_text: Is every locally flat topological embedding of a closed nonorientable surface in S4 whose complement has fundamental group of order 2 homeomorphic to one of the embeddings obtained from the involution on aCP2 # bCP2 with fixed set #a+bRP2?

evidence.quote: The involution on aCP2#bCP2 thus gives a locally flat embedding of #a+bRP2 in S4.
Conjecture. Any locally flat topological embedding of a closed nonorientable surface in S 4 whose complement has order 2 fundamental group is homeomorphic to one of the above embeddings.

accepted.question_text: For a finitely presented group π and ε ∈ {±1}, call g0 an ε-genus cancellation bound if every compact smooth 2q-manifold M with ε = (−1)^q, π1(M) ≅ π, and genus g(M) at least g0 satisfies cancellation, meaning that every manifold stably diffeomorphic to M with the same Euler characteristic is actually diffeomorphic to M; let cgε(π) be the least such g0, or ∞ if none exists. Is there a finitely presented group π that is not polycyclic-by-finite and nevertheless has cgε(π) < ∞ for some ε?
accepted.context_brief: Cancellation genus bounds for general groups

evidence.quote: We say that g0 is a ε-genus cancellation bound for π if cancellation holds for every 2q-manifold M with ε = (−1)q, π1(M)∼= π and genus g(M)≥ g0. If such a g0 exists, the ε-cancellation genus of π is defined to be minimum genus cancellation bound cgε (π).
Problem A. (Genus bounds for general groups) Is there an example of a finitely presented group π which is not polycyclic-by-finite and for which cgε (π) < ∞ for some ε?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a finitely presented group π and ε ∈ {±1} with cancellation genus cgε(π) at least 2, equivalently a pair of 2q-manifolds M and N with π1(M) ≅ π1(N) ≅ π such that M # Wg is diffeomorphic to N # Wg for some g but M # W1 and N # W1 are not diffeomorphic?
accepted.context_brief: Whether cancellation genus can exceed one

evidence.quote: there are no known examples where cgε (π)≥ 2; i.e. the following problem is still open.

Problem B. (Is the cancellation genus ever greater than one?) Is there a finitely presented group π and ε∈{± 1} such that cgε (π)≥ 2? i.e. is there a pair of 2q-manifolds M and N with π1(M)∼= π1(M)∼= π such that we have M♯Wg∼= N♯Wg for some g but M♯W1 and N♯W1 are not diffeomorphic?

accepted.question_text: Let M be a connected closed 2q-manifold with fundamental group π and orientation character w1. The Wall realization action of L2q+1(Z[π], w1) acts on the stable class Sst(M) of manifolds stably diffeomorphic to M with the same Euler characteristic. Determine the orbit set Sst(M)/L2q+1(Z[π], w1).
accepted.context_brief: Orbit set of the stable class under Wall realization

evidence.quote: Recall that π = π1(M) and w1 = w1(M) ... the L-group L2q+1(Z[π],w1) acts on the stable class of M via Wall realisation: S st(M)× L2q+1(Z[π],w1)→ S st(M).
Problem. Determine S st(M)/L2q+1(Z[π],w1), the set of orbits of the action of L2q+1(Z[π],w1) on the stable class.

accepted.question_text: Fix q ≥ 3. Suppose (M0, ν̄0) and (M1, ν̄1) are 2q-dimensional normal (q−1)-smoothings over a fibration ξ : B → BO, are (B, ξ)-bordant, have equal Euler characteristic, and have isometric extended quadratic Qξ(q)-forms. Must they differ by the action of L2q+1(Z[π], w1))? Equivalently, is the map μ from NSξ(M, ν̄)/L2q+1(Z[π], w1) to the set of isometry classes of Qξ(q)-forms injective?

evidence.quote: Hence the map above descends to define the map µ: NS ξ (M, ¯ν)/L2q+1(Z[π],w1)→ Hom(Z[π],w1)(Qξ (q)).

Conjecture A. (The Q-form Conjecture for normal smoothings) If q≥ 3, then the map µ of (2) is injective; i.e. if q≥ 3 and (M0, ¯ν0) and (M1, ¯ν1) are 2 q-dimensional (B, ξ )-bordant normal (q−1)-smoothings with equal Euler characteristic and isometric Qξ (q)-forms, then (M0, ¯ν0) and (M1, ¯ν1) differ by the action of L2q+1(Z[π],w1).

accepted.question_text: Fix q ≥ 3 and let ξq−1_M represent the normal (q−1)-type of a connected closed 2q-manifold M. If M0 and M1 lie in the stable class Sst(M), does the isometry class of the associated Qξq−1_M(q)-forms, modulo the action of aut(ξq−1_M), determine whether M0 and M1 differ by the Wall realization action of L2q+1(Z[π], w1)? Equivalently, is the map μ/aut(ξ) from Sst(M)/L2q+1(Z[π], w1) to Hom(Z[π], w1)(Qξq−1_M(q))/aut(ξq−1_M) injective?
accepted.context_brief: Q-form Conjecture for the stable class

evidence.quote: when ξ = ξ q−1 M is a representative of the normal (q−1)-type of M, the map µ/aut(ξ ) induces another map ... µ/aut(ξ ) : S st(M)/L2q+1(Z[π],w1)→ Hom(Z[π],w1)(Qξ q−1 M (q))/aut(ξ q−1 M ).
Conjecture B. (The Q-form Conjecture for the stable class) If q≥ 3, then the map µ/aut(ξ ) of (3) is injective
M0∼= ρM1 for some ρ∈ L2q+1(Z[π],w1) if and only if for i = 0,1, there are normal (q−1)-smoothings ¯νi : Mi→ Bq−1 M such that µ(M0, ¯ν0) and µ(M1, ¯ν1) are isometric Qξ q−1 M (q)-forms.
